title: Admin Microtask Orchestrator: telemetry-driven synthetic playbooks with HL-in-the-loop escalation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight Admin Microtask Orchestrator (AMO) that converts common runbook steps into composable microtasks, executes synthetic playbooks driven by live telemetry, and escalates to human-in-the-loop (HL) flows when confidence or safety checks fail.

Scope:
- Define a microtask schema for idempotent, observable steps (checks, reads, writes, rollbacks).
- Implement an execution engine that can run tasks locally on operator workstations or as ephemeral cloud workers.
- Integrate with existing KV cache and ops telemetry to seed synthetic playbook runs (replay recent traces at safe speed).
- Provide a policy layer for automatic short-circuit (auto-fix) vs HL escalation based on confidence thresholds and safety validators.
- Expose task invocation via Console command palette and an ops CLI (opsctl).

Success criteria:
- 80% of high-frequency postmortem actions can be expressed as microtasks.
- Synthetic playbook dry-runs detect regressions in 90% of sampled incidents before customer impact.
- Mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for routine incidents reduced by >= 25% in pilot org.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Execution surface: embedding tasks inside a single process minimizes orchestration overhead but increases blast radius. We opted for an ephemeral worker model (containerized task runner) so each task is isolated and has fine-grained RBAC.
- Language and portability: tasks authored as small JS modules (Node 18) to match existing ops scripts and enable dynamic loading in Console and CLI. Downsides: dependency management and sandboxing needs careful handling.
- Safety model: rely on preconditions/assertions, dry-run mode, and a mandatory two-step commit for write actions that affect production (preview -> apply). This increases latency for writes but greatly reduces unsafe automations.

Telemetry & observability:
- Task runs emit structured events to the ops telemetry pipeline: task_start, task_end, task_error, precondition_failed, dryrun_result, apply_result.
- Dashboard tracking: per-task success rate, median runtime, error-rate by operator, and correlated incident reduction.
- Canary metric: rollout begins with pilot group (SRE & Platform Eng). Target error-rate <= 1% on dry-runs and <= 0.1% on apply for pilot team.

Rollout plan:
1) Alpha (2 weeks): internal dev-only; basic engine and 8 seed microtasks (cache-warm, trace-collect, shard-restart-simulate, config-check, key-rotate-preview).
2) Beta (4 weeks): pilot with SRE; enable synthetic playbook scheduler to replay 48-hour incident traces at 20% speed.
3) Gradual rollout (6 weeks): opt-in across platform teams; add RBAC scopes and limit apply to two-person approvals.

Open risks & mitigation:
- Risk: accidental writes from synthetic runs. Mitigation: all synthetic playbacks are dry-run-only by default; apply requires explicit confirmation and must pass safety validators.
- Risk: task library sprawl. Mitigation: publish curated starter tasks and require PR review + test harness for new tasks.
- Risk: performance overhead for telemetry injection. Mitigation: sample traces and provide a low-overhead instrumentation mode.

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- PR: initial engine and microtask schema (github.com/redwood-inference/opsctl/pull/412) — awaiting design review from @izabela (comments requested 2026-02-22).
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/AMO-Design-Spec (draft)
- Drive artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1cAMO-playbooks (seed tasks and example manifests).
- Security review request raised: SEC-REQ-2026-013 (workspace: security), scheduled 2026-03-12.

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- Engine merged behind feature flag, 8 seed tasks merged, telemetry events emitted to ops-prod, policy validators in place, and pilot runbook executed end-to-end without manual rollback in pilot SRE org.
